title: Temperatures recorded in a city of Madhya Pradesh
body: A student copied the following daily temperature readings for a city in Madhya Pradesh from a weather chart. Each row gives the date, then the maximum temperature and the minimum temperature recorded that day (in degrees Celsius). 28.02.2025: maximum 29, minimum 16. 01.03.2025: maximum 30, minimum 15. 02.03.2025: maximum 31, minimum 17. 03.03.2025: maximum 32, minimum 18. 04.03.2025: maximum 30, minimum 17. 05.03.2025: maximum 28, minimum 14. 06.03.2025: maximum 29, minimum 15. The student's teacher reminded the class that the range of temperature is the maximum temperature minus the minimum temperature during a period, and that the mean daily temperature is the maximum plus the minimum temperature of the day divided by two.

title: A weather warning for a coastal state
body: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issues weather maps that show each area with one of four levels: No Warning; Watch (Be Updated); Alert (Be Prepared); and Warning (Take Action). Small icons on the map show the type of weather expected, such as heavy rain, strong surface winds, thunder and lightning, or a heat wave. Imagine that on one day in May such a map shows three districts of a coastal state as follows. District P lies on the sea coast. It is marked 'Warning (Take Action)' with icons for strong surface winds and extremely heavy rain, because a low-pressure system over the sea is expected to become a cyclone. Barometers there read below 1000 mb and are still falling. District Q lies in the plains about 150 km inland. It is marked 'Alert (Be Prepared)' with an icon for heavy rain. District R lies in the hills further inland and is marked 'No Warning'.
